title: 29.5 A 3nm 3.6GHz Dual-Port SRAM with Backend-RC Optimization and a Far-End Write-Assist Scheme
problem: Dual-port SRAM design at 3nm process nodes suffers from increased resistance-capacitance (RC) degradation, complex timing constraints from asynchronous dual-clock operation, and challenges maintaining write margins across wide voltage/temperature ranges.
motivation: Dual-port SRAMs enable higher read/write bandwidth from multiple clock domains, but aggressive scaling exacerbates RC effects and design complexity, requiring novel circuit techniques to maintain reliability and speed.
method: The design combines array dual-rail (ADR) voltage management with VDI for periphery and VDDM for cell arrays, introduces a far-end write-assist scheme to strengthen write margins, and updates wakeup circuitry to handle complex voltage relationships (VDD > VDDM > VSS constraints).
key_novelty: Far-end write-assist scheme integrated with array dual-rail voltage management for robust dual-port SRAM operation at 3nm.
contributions: Design-technology co-optimization opportunities enabling better area scaling than single-port SRAM
Far-end write-assist circuit for sub-500mV write-margin operation
Refined wakeup scheme for array dual-rail voltage management
20kb DP-SRAM demonstrating 495mV minimum operating voltage at 95% yield (−40°C) and 3.6GHz operation at 1.0V
limitations: Evaluation at single technology node (3nm); scaling to 2nm and lower not discussed.
primary_theme: Dual-port SRAM with far-end write-assist for ultra-low-voltage 3nm operation
